Messages.Author: Mangaser
Messages.Body:
I just read through LSJ's revised rules posted a few days ago and had a bunch
of questions - oh, btw, if it matters, we play with a 4CL house rule (makes
everyone happy) -

1. Regarding withdrawing from the game, there's a conflict between what's
written in the online revised rules (victory point for successful withdrawal)
and the Sabbat rules insert (forced withdrawal, no VP involved). Which rule is
to be followed?

2. When exactly does your grand-prey become your prey? Is it immediately
after you oust your prey or immediately after your turn is over? For example,
can I (without the use of D-bleeds) bleed out my prey with one vampire (ousting
him) then bleed the next player with another vampire? Or do I have to wait
till after my turn before my grand-prey becomes my "official" prey?

3. Regarding contesting cards with yourself, I want to see if my
interpretation is correct. I have Igo#1 in play. I bring another Igo(#2) in
play and this results in both being contested. My following turn, I pay one
pool to keep Igo#2 and yield Igo#1 by burning it. I get control of Igo#2 at
the beginning of my next turn, and not immediately, correct?

4. When do you replace votes dropped from your hands (called "push votes," I
believe) - immediately after the vote or at the end of the current minion
phase? Can you use these political cards as votes in all types of referendums
(vote to burn Elysium, Blood Hunt, etc.)? I realize that a Blood Hunt is not
an action so no Reactions or Modifiers are allowed, but are push votes allowed?

5. I read the section on hand damage vs. damage from weapons based on hand
damage. Does this mean that Torn Signpost and Brass Knuckles can't work in
conjunction?

6. Am I correct in assuming that the wording on V:tES cards overrules the
wording on the corresponding Jyhad cards?

7. Does a Dodge prevent Steal Blood Strikes?

8. I read through the aggravated damage and am now thoroughly confused. Are
these online rules the most recent ruling on the matter? Let me see if I have
this straight, according to these online rules:

Situation A - 1 pt. of agg. on a vampire with at least one blood.
Result - vampire in torpor with the same blood total.

Situation B - 1 pt. of agg. on a vampire with no blood.
Result - vampire in torpor with no blood.

Situation C - 2 pt. of agg. on a vampire with x blood, where x is greater than
or equal to 1.
Result - vampire in torpor with x-1 blood.

Situation D - 1 pt. regular, 1 pt. agg. to vampire with 1 blood.
Result - vampire burned.

Situation E - 1 pt. regular, 1 pt. agg. to vampire with 2 blood.
Result - vampire in torpor with 1 blood.

If A, B, C, and E are true, we've been playing the game all wrong. :(

9. A card question on Blood to Water. My interpretation was that a vampire
would burn 3 blood at basic (or all if it had 3 or less blood) and an ally or
such would be burned. Is my interpretation correct?

10. Ten is a nice round number, so I just want to thank everyone in advance.
I think I know the answers to most of these, but I want to be sure with this
tournament coming up. It's also really hard for someone new like me to get
straight answers without knowing where to go and if any current, up-to-date
standardized rules exist (see my question regarding the conflict between Sabbat
inserts and online docs) and who has the final say on things. Any help on this
matter is much appreciated. Thanks again for your time!

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <19981011014353...@ng31.aol.com>, Mangaser
<mang...@aol.com> writes

>1. Regarding withdrawing from the game, there's a conflict between what's
>written in the online revised rules (victory point for successful withdrawal)
>and the Sabbat rules insert (forced withdrawal, no VP involved). Which rule is
>to be followed?
>

The Sabbat rules are *highly* optional. It is suspected that Wizards
introduced it to try and speed up the game, maknig it more like Magic.
Bad move. :(

In general, the online revised rules are best AND the official rules.
However, if you want to play the Sabbat Rules (or anything else you care
to use) you are quite welcome to.

>2. When exactly does your grand-prey become your prey? Is it immediately
>after you oust your prey or immediately after your turn is over?

Immediately after you oust your prey. Your prey is always the player to
your left. When you oust your current prey, the player to your left is
your previous grand prey.

To be honest, I've never seen why people have a problem with this one.

> For example,
>can I (without the use of D-bleeds)

(D) bleeds can only be directed at your prey unless there is card text
which specifies otherwise.

>bleed out my prey with one vampire (ousting
>him) then bleed the next player with another vampire?

Yes, you can. Players A, B, C in a circle. The moment player B is
ousted, player A can bleed player C normally because they are now their
prey.

> Or do I have to wait
>till after my turn before my grand-prey becomes my "official" prey?

Why are they not your official prey now?

>
>3. Regarding contesting cards with yourself, I want to see if my
>interpretation is correct. I have Igo#1 in play. I bring another Igo(#2) in
>play and this results in both being contested. My following turn, I pay one
>pool to keep Igo#2 and yield Igo#1 by burning it. I get control of Igo#2 at
>the beginning of my next turn, and not immediately, correct?

Correct. (I think). Check with LSJ.

>
>4. When do you replace votes dropped from your hands (called "push votes," I
>believe) - immediately after the vote or at the end of the current minion
>phase?

The rules have changed on this. You may only throw down 1 political
card to "push" a vote. This is designed to limit Weenie Vote Push (an
evil deck archetype). If you called the vote with a political action
card (ie NOT using a card in play like Elysium) then that political card
IS your one political card. The idea was to make political decks need
more thought and require cards like Bewitching Oration, The Mausoleum,
Power Structure and so forth, or permanent votes from vampires.

Because of this change to something more sensible, they are replaced at
the end of the vote.

>Can you use these political cards as votes in all types of referendums
>(vote to burn Elysium, Blood Hunt, etc.)?

Yes.

>I realize that a Blood Hunt is not
>an action so no Reactions or Modifiers are allowed, but are push votes allowed?

Push votes - no, since push votes implies throwing more than 1 political
card down from your hand. However, you (like any other Methuselah) are
entitled to throw down 1 political card to vote on the vote.

>
>5. I read the section on hand damage vs. damage from weapons based on hand
>damage. Does this mean that Torn Signpost and Brass Knuckles can't work in
>conjunction?

No, they will. Torn Signpost sets your hand damage to 2/3. Brass
Knuckles then adds to that AND THEN makes it melee weapon damage. This
means that other cards, which alter the other properties of your hand
damage, won't work on the Brass Knuckles.

Something like Wolf Claws:

For the remainder of the round, this vampire's hand
damage is aggravated.

won't work with Brass Knuckles because the vampire is now dealing melee
weapon damage, not hand damage. But, a weapon will take the amount of
hand damage you do and add to that, yes. Otherwise a Bastard Sword
would only do 1 damage, and not two, because it wouldn't add to your in
built 1 hand damage.

>
>6. Am I correct in assuming that the wording on V:tES cards overrules the
>wording on the corresponding Jyhad cards?
>

In general, yes. And Sabbat over-rules them.

However, check the errata because sometimes the V:TES text is fluffed or
has been changed for whatever reason. Errata/Rulings/Clarifications
have the final word.

>7. Does a Dodge prevent Steal Blood Strikes?
>

Prevent in the sense of "I lose no blood" then yes.

>8. I read through the aggravated damage and am now thoroughly confused. Are
>these online rules the most recent ruling on the matter? Let me see if I have
>this straight, according to these online rules:
>
>Situation A - 1 pt. of agg. on a vampire with at least one blood.
>Result - vampire in torpor with the same blood total.
>

Correct

>Situation B - 1 pt. of agg. on a vampire with no blood.
>Result - vampire in torpor with no blood.
>

Correct.

>Situation C - 2 pt. of agg. on a vampire with x blood, where x is greater than
>or equal to 1.
>Result - vampire in torpor with x-1 blood.
>

Correct.

>Situation D - 1 pt. regular, 1 pt. agg. to vampire with 1 blood.
>Result - vampire burned.
>

Incorrect. Result: vampire in torpor with 0 blood.

>Situation E - 1 pt. regular, 1 pt. agg. to vampire with 2 blood.
>Result - vampire in torpor with 1 blood.
>

Correct.

>If A, B, C, and E are true, we've been playing the game all wrong. :(
>

No, the rules were errataed to prevent Ivory Bow et al being so
powerful. In Jyhad, it was almost impossible to burn a vampire with
them. In V:TES, it became too easy.

>9. A card question on Blood to Water. My interpretation was that a vampire
>would burn 3 blood at basic (or all if it had 3 or less blood) and an ally or
>such would be burned. Is my interpretation correct?

Correct. If a vampire had only 2 blood, it would burn it all but would
not be burned.

>
>10. Ten is a nice round number, so I just want to thank everyone in advance.
>I think I know the answers to most of these, but I want to be sure with this
>tournament coming up. It's also really hard for someone new like me to get
>straight answers without knowing where to go and if any current, up-to-date
>standardized rules exist (see my question regarding the conflict between Sabbat
>inserts and online docs) and who has the final say on things.

LSJ, in all cases, has the final say on things.

> Correct

> >Situation C - 2 pt. of agg. on a vampire with x blood, where x is greater than
> >or equal to 1.

> Correct

Actually, if you want to be pedantic about it, aggravated damage always
gets resolved after normal damage. So, the first point of regular damage
burns one blood to heal (leaving the vamp at 0 blood) and then becomes
the same as example B (above), ie takes one point of agg and is sent to
torpor with zero blood.

I'm not sure whether this order of events is crucial anymore since the
agg. damage rules are back to being x+1 to burn, but previously it had a
big impact if blood was stolen, burned or whatever.

Martin.

guenh...@mindspring.com wrote:
> >5. I read the section on hand damage vs. damage from weapons based on hand
> >damage. Does this mean that Torn Signpost and Brass Knuckles can't work in
> >conjunction?
>
> No, they do combine, and the resulting strike would be with Brass
> Knuckles (a melee weapon strike) for modified base hand damage plus
> one.

I'm not sure I agree with this. The Jyhad printing of this card would infer
that you could use the two together. The VTES version specifies using
"hand damage as a strike" which, by the definition of hand damage,
precludes the minion from using a melee weapon. Logically, if a vampire
is beating you with a torn signpost, his bastard sword (or whatever) will
only get in the way.

However, there is currently errata (below with other relevant data) that
states that Torn Signpost only sets the base hand damage, which means that
the above response is correct. Personally, I'd like to see this errata
overturned in favor of VTES card text to remove the contradiction of the
definition of hand damage and the way the card is played.

Noal McDonald

VTES Text:
Only usable before range is determined. This vampire can inflict 2 hand
damage as a strike for remainder of the combat.
(S) As above, but vampire can inflict 3 hand damage as a strike for the
remainder of the combat.

Jyhad Text:
Play before range is determined. This vampire does 2 hand damage for
remainder of the combat.
(S) As Above, but vampire does 3 hand damage for the remainder of
the combat.

Torn Signpost - combat (pot)
Sets a vampire's base hand damage to 2 (or 3 if superior). [TOM 960306]

Damage (Combat)
Hand damage: damage from a hand strike. e.g. Damage from a Bastard Sword
is *not* hand damage. [LSJ 970224]

Mangaser wrote:
>
> I just read through LSJ's revised rules posted a few days ago and had a bunch
> of questions - oh, btw, if it matters, we play with a 4CL house rule (makes
> everyone happy)

Thanks for the input, but your choice of house rules (4CL in this
case) doesn't change the answers to questions on the revised
rulebook. :-)

> 1. Regarding withdrawing from the game, there's a conflict between what's
> written in the online revised rules (victory point for successful withdrawal)
> and the Sabbat rules insert (forced withdrawal, no VP involved). Which rule is
> to be followed?

The revised rules. The Sabbat rules were relegated to "optional"
status almost immediately upon being issued, is not sooner.

> 2. When exactly does your grand-prey become your prey? Is it immediately
> after you oust your prey or immediately after your turn is over?

As soon as she becomes the player to your left (the definition
of "prey") - that is, immediately.

> For example,
> can I (without the use of D-bleeds) bleed out my prey with one vampire (ousting

All bleeds are D, and they all must target your prey by default unless
explicit card text overrides that restriction.

> him) then bleed the next player with another vampire? Or do I have to wait

> till after my turn before my grand-prey becomes my "official" prey?

The player to your left is always your official prey. When someone
is ousted, her predator will immediately find a new player seated in
the "prey" position (to her left).

> 3. Regarding contesting cards with yourself, I want to see if my
> interpretation is correct. I have Igo#1 in play. I bring another Igo(#2) in
> play and this results in both being contested. My following turn, I pay one
> pool to keep Igo#2 and yield Igo#1 by burning it. I get control of Igo#2 at
> the beginning of my next turn, and not immediately, correct?

Correct.

> 4. When do you replace votes dropped from your hands (called "push votes," I

"push votes" normally refers to *additional* political action cards
burned for votes (after the first one by the same player), which is
no longer allowable. Since there is no "old-school" push anymore,
is see no reason now not to refer to "political action cards burned
for votes" as "push votes" for convenience, however.

> believe) - immediately after the vote or at the end of the current minion
> phase?

Immediately after the referendum.

> Can you use these political cards as votes in all types of referendums
> (vote to burn Elysium, Blood Hunt, etc.)? I realize that a Blood Hunt is not
> an action so no Reactions or Modifiers are allowed, but are push votes allowed?

Yes.

> 5. I read the section on hand damage vs. damage from weapons based on hand
> damage. Does this mean that Torn Signpost and Brass Knuckles can't work in
> conjunction?

No. Torn Signpost resets the vampire's strength to 3. Brass Knuckles
inflict strength+1 damage when used as a strike. The two are usable
with each other.

> 6. Am I correct in assuming that the wording on V:tES cards overrules the
> wording on the corresponding Jyhad cards?

Yes, unless errata has been issued to the contrary (like in the case
of Torn Signpost, for example: [TOM 06-MAR-98])

> 7. Does a Dodge prevent Steal Blood Strikes?

Unless the latter was directed at a retainer, yes.

> 8. I read through the aggravated damage and am now thoroughly confused. Are
> these online rules the most recent ruling on the matter?

Yes.

> Let me see if I have
> this straight, according to these online rules:
>
> Situation A - 1 pt. of agg. on a vampire with at least one blood.
> Result - vampire in torpor with the same blood total.

Correct. The agg damage cannot be healed, so the vampire
doesn't burn blood trying to heal. Since he has unhealed
damage, he will go to torpor.

> Situation B - 1 pt. of agg. on a vampire with no blood.
> Result - vampire in torpor with no blood.

Correct, same reasoning.

> Situation C - 2 pt. of agg. on a vampire with x blood, where x is greater than
> or equal to 1.
> Result - vampire in torpor with x-1 blood.

Right. The first point is handled as above. The second point, since
it is done to a vampire that already has unhealed damage, will burn
the vampire unless the vampire burns a blood to prevent destruction.

> Situation D - 1 pt. regular, 1 pt. agg. to vampire with 1 blood.
> Result - vampire burned.

No. The regular damage is healable, so the vampire burns a blood
to heal it, leaving himself with zero blood. The agg damage
cannot be healed, so the vampire doesn't burn a blood trying to
heal. And he doesn't yet have unhealed damage, so the agg won't
burn him, either. He will go to torpor, empty, since he has
unhealed damage, however.

> Situation E - 1 pt. regular, 1 pt. agg. to vampire with 2 blood.
> Result - vampire in torpor with 1 blood.

Right, as above.

> If A, B, C, and E are true, we've been playing the game all wrong. :(

This is a change from the previous version of the aggravated
damage rules (the ones printed in the V:TES rulebook).

> 9. A card question on Blood to Water. My interpretation was that a vampire
> would burn 3 blood at basic (or all if it had 3 or less blood) and an ally or
> such would be burned. Is my interpretation correct?

Yes.

> 10. Ten is a nice round number, so I just want to thank everyone in advance.
> I think I know the answers to most of these, but I want to be sure with this
> tournament coming up. It's also really hard for someone new like me to get
> straight answers without knowing where to go and if any current, up-to-date
> standardized rules exist (see my question regarding the conflict between Sabbat
> inserts and online docs) and who has the final say on things. Any help on this
> matter is much appreciated. Thanks again for your time!

The revised rules supercede all previous rulebooks, including the
Sabbat rulesheet. The final rules authority for the game is me,
L. Scott Johnson. Compilations of rulings and clarifications (like
your Blood to Water question and the Torn Signpost errata) can be
found from the Wizards' VTES rules page (linked in my .sig below).

Martin Jamieson wrote:

> Richard D. Zopf wrote:
> > >Situation D - 1 pt. regular, 1 pt. agg. to vampire with 1 blood.
> > >Result - vampire burned.
> > Incorrect. The first point of agg. damage sends the vampire to torpor
> > without the loss of a blood. The regular point of damage removes one
> > blood, as normal. Result; vampire in torpor with no blood.
> >
>

> Actually, if you want to be pedantic about it, aggravated damage always
> gets resolved after normal damage. So, the first point of regular damage
> burns one blood to heal (leaving the vamp at 0 blood) and then becomes
> the same as example B (above), ie takes one point of agg and is sent to
> torpor with zero blood.
>
> I'm not sure whether this order of events is crucial anymore since the
> agg. damage rules are back to being x+1 to burn, but previously it had a
> big impact if blood was stolen, burned or whatever.

It is still crucial, since it is not exactly X+1 to burn (noticable
when a mix of regular and aggravated damage is done).

The basic rule is: A point of agg damage done to a vampire with
unhealed damage (or otherwise on his way to or already in torpor)
will burn him unless he burns a blood to prevent destruction.
And aggravated damage cannot be healed.

So, if a vampire sustains more regular damage than he can heal (i.e.,
more than X regular damage) and one point of aggravated, then he
will burn all of his blood (X) healing some (X) of the regular damage.
The rest of the regular damage will remain unhealed.
The single point of agg, since the vampire has unhealed damage
already, will burn the vampire, unless he burns a blood to prevent
destruction (which he cannot do, since he has already spent all of
his blood).

No. It was to restore the original intended power level of aggravated
damage. Certainly, the VTES rules were easier to understand.

The new rules are even harder to understand because the old simple rule
got players used to equating blood with damage, which was never the case.

Damage and burning blood are two separate things.

Under the old VTES rules:
You take damage and then (if you're a vampire) you
burn blood to heal the damage (or, in the case of
aggravated damage, you don't burn a blood to heal,
since agg damage cannot be healed. Instead, the
aggravated damage will burn you unless you burn a
blood to prevent destruction). Note that healing
damage and preventing destruction are two distinct
things, even though both are accomplished by burning
blood.

The new rules are the same as the above, except that
aggravated damage won't burn a healthy (undamaged,
un-torpored) vampire. It will burn a wounded
(on-his-way-to-torpor or in-torpor) vampire, however,
unless he burns a blood to prevent destruction.

> In all the messages that I've seen previously, it says that the first
> point of agg damage doesn't cause the vamp to burn a blood because it
> can't be healed.

"First point" is irrelevant. The first, middle, and last points of
aggravated damage cannot be healed. No blood is spent healing damage
that cannot be healed.

The first, middle, and last points of aggravated damage will burn
a wounded vampire. A wounded vampire must burn a blood to prevent
destruction from each of these points.

> Yet you say that "The single point of agg, since the
> vampire has unhealed damage already, will burn the vampire, unless he
> burns a blood to prevent destruction". If the first point of agg damage
> doesn't cause the vamp to burn a blood (because he can't), why is it

It *does* require him to burn a blood if he is damaged.
Not to heal, of course, since it cannot be healed, but
rather to prevent destruction since it will burn his
damaged body if he doesn't burn a blood.

> that if he doesn't burn a blood in the above example, he burns? It seems
> like a contradiction to me.

Since preventing destruction is not the same as healing damage,
this is not a contradiction.

It IS really very simple...
you just deal with the damage one point at a time, and there are 4
cases (ready or torpored vamp, normal or aggro damage):

a ready vampire takes one point of damage. If the vampire has blood
left, she burns one blood. If not, she goes to torpor.

a ready vampire takes one point of aggro damage. She goes to torpor.

a torpored vamp takes one point of normal damage. If the vampire has
blood left, he burns one blood. If not, nothing happens.

a torpored vamp takes one point of aggro damage. If the vampire has
blood left, he burns one blood. If not, he is burned.

Maybe it's just because I'm a computer science major, but when you
break it down into a few very simple rules it all becomes easy to
understand.

This may not be how the rules were explained, but following these
rules will give you the correct results, and it makes it clear what is
going on as you take damage.

agen...@my-dejanews.com wrote:

: > Damage will wound a vampire.

: 1 aggravated damage.
: Yet the above makes it seem like that is not the case.

It's not, at least not exactly (I'm not sure what post you're referring to).
A vampire is not 'wounded' just because it's burning blood to heal damage.
A vampire is 'wounded' if it has taken damage that it could not heal. That
is, if it took a point of normal damage when it had no blood, and was
therefore unable to heal it, or if it took a point of agg damage, which
can never be healed.

When a vampire is not 'wounded', each point of normal damage it takes
requires it to burn a blood or else become 'wounded'. Each point of
agg damage it takes causes it to become 'wounded', since vampires cannot
heal agg damage. The confusion seems to arise because typically, if a
vampire takes multiple points of agg damage, the first one will cause
that vamp to become 'wounded', and agg damage affects 'wounded' vampires
differently than normal damage (and differently than agg damage affects
non-'wounded' vampires).

When a vampire *is* 'wounded', each point of agg damage it takes requires
it to burn a blood or else be burned. Each point of normal damage requires
it to burn a blood as usual; if it can't, nothing happens (since the vamp
is already 'wounded').

So if a previously unwounded vamp takes 2 regular and 1 agg, it is handled
like this: First point of regular: vamp burns a blood or becomes wounded.
Second point of regular: vamp burns a blood or becomes wounded.
First point of agg: vamp becomes wounded (if it wasn't already)
or must burn a blood to avoid being destroyed (if the regular damage caused
it to become wounded).

: So the *only* way that a vampire will *ever* burn a blood due to agg

: damage is if there is more than 1 point of agg damage done to that vampire
: irregardless of how much normal damage was done to that vampire (that
: doesn't reduce that vampire to 0 blood)?

No, that's not quite correct. A vamp must burn blood to avoid destruction
whenever it takes agg damage *if it is already wounded*. If it is not
previously wounded, a point of agg damage will cause the vamp to become
wounded, but will not require burning a blood to avoid destruction.

This is why there is a functional difference between 'the first point'
of agg and 'further points' of agg. The reason 'first point' terminology
is not used is because there is no 'packeting' or 'single source' effect
inherent in the current damage rules.

The 'wounded' terminology is (I believe) new to this set of damage rules.
It might take a little getting used to, but I think it's the best way to
explain how these rules really work.

Josh

"To illustrate what I was saying, a 5/5 vamp takes 4 damage (damage that

This is correct. What you seem to be misunderstanding is the correct useage of
the term "wounded". A "wounded" vampire is specificaly a vampire on the way to
torpor. Not a vampire who takes damage. Not a vampire with a wound. Very
specifically a vampire who is currently on the way to torpor. Nothing else
covers the term "wounded" in this discussion. If a vampire is currently on the
way to torpor, it is wounded. If it is not on the way to torpor, it is not
wounded.

There are two ways to become wounded. A) Take a point of aggrivated damage
(when you have not previously taken one), B) Take more regular (non aggrivated)
damage than you have blood to burn. Thus, a vampire with 8 blood who takes one
point of aggro damage becomes wounded (as he is on the way to torpor). A
vampire with 4 blood who is hit for 5 or more regular damage becomes wounded
(as he is on the way to torpor). (I am fairly certain that a vampire who is
torporized by something like Coma also counts as wounded for this discussion,
so there would be three ways to become wounded, but that doesn't really matter
here).

"However, this begs the question, if that same vamp (in the same circumstances)
takes 5 damage and 1 agg damage, does the vamp burn. If I understand this
correctly, I say no. It simply drops to Torpor."

You are correct. The vampire starts with 5 blood. He takes 5 regular damage,
reducing him to 0 blood. A vampire with 0 blood does not go to torpor, so he
is not wounded (as he is not currently going to torpor). Then he takes the 1
aggro damage (as you always apply regular damage first). As he is not wounded
(i.e. currently going to torpor), a point of aggrivated damage does not cause
you to burn blood, but it does send you to torpor (wounds you). If in the
above situation, the vampire took 6 regular damage and 1 aggro, he _would_
burn, as the 6 points would send the vampire to torpor (wounding him) and then
the one point of aggro damage would require him to burn a blood to avoid
destruction, as he is already wounded (on the way to torpor) when he takes the
aggro damage. As he has no blood to burn, poof.

Remember. Wounded means "currently on the way to torpor". It means nothing
else in this discussion.

On VTES-L, Krzysztof Meyer writes:
> I want to ask about only one example with aggr damage.
> New vamp becomes controlled. She is capacity 3. Right after other

> capacity vamp. She suffers 4 aggro in combat. Will she be burnt

Not. Resolve each point in turn:

1) Done to a healthy vampire. Cannot be healed, but won't destroy
a healthy vampire. So no blood is burned to heal (impossible) or
to prevent destruction (not applicable).
The vampire is now on her way to torpor, since she has unhealed
damage. We'll call "en route to torpor" "wounded" for brevity.
2) Done to a "wounded" vampire. Will destroy a wounded vampire, so
the vampire must burn one blood to prevent destruction. (She now
has 2 blood left). She is still on her way to torpor.
3) Done to a "wounded" vampire. Will destroy a wounded vampire, so
the vampire must burn one blood to prevent destruction. (She now
has 1 blood left). She is still on her way to torpor.
4) Done to a "wounded" vampire. Will destroy a wounded vampire, so
the vampire must burn one blood to prevent destruction. (She now
has 0 blood left). She is still on her way to torpor.

At the end of strike resolution, the vampire goes to torpor (empty).
